title: High School 5K Times: Freshman vs. Senior Year
text:
Summary
Comparing the two distributions reveals a clear difference in average 5K time improvement between men and women from freshman to senior year. Men improved substantially on average, dropping 1 minute and 12 seconds from 19:34 as freshmen to 18:22 as seniors (with 87% of male runners recording a faster senior time, visible in the clear leftward shift of the red dots). In contrast, women showed a much smaller average improvement of 9 seconds, moving from 22:36 to 22:28 (with 59% running faster as seniors and the freshman and senior distributions largely overlapping).
Data Source: Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) District Cross Country Championship results (2011–2020), archived on Baum’s Page.

title: Future: Collegiate Running
text:
This page follows standout high school athletes from our dataset who transitioned to collegiate cross country. In college competition, men typically race the 8K (8,000 meters) and women race the 6K (6,000 meters).
Predictions are based on Pete Riegel’s classic race prediction model (\(T_2 = T_1 \times (D_2 / D_1)^{1.06}\)), projecting the athlete’s collegiate time from their high school senior 5K mark.

title: About
text:
About This Project
This project explores how high school cross country runners’ 5K race times evolve as athletes progress from their freshman to senior years. By tracking individual athletes across multiple seasons, this project investigates how physiological maturity, training, and gender relate to distance-running development. Beyond overall distribution shifts, the website examines individual standout performances, the diverse Ohio race courses and terrain conditions athletes encounter, and how high school runners transition to collegiate distances.

Methodology

Data Collection: Longitudinal race records were compiled from Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) cross country championship meets between 2011 and 2020, archived on Baum’s Page.
Cohort Pairing: The analysis focuses on a balanced cohort of 2,000 runners (1,000 men and 1,000 women). Each runner has matched official 5K times from both their freshman and senior championship seasons to allow direct within-athlete paired comparisons.
Performance Metrics: Race times recorded as text strings (MM:SS) were converted into elapsed seconds to calculate exact individual progression (\(\text{Improvement} = \text{Freshman Time} - \text{Senior Time}\)). Positive values represent time dropped (running faster).
Analytical & Visual Tools: Built with R and Quarto using the tidyverse. Interactive stacked dotplots using Plotly enable readers to inspect full time distributions and trace paired freshman-to-senior trajectories for any individual runner.



Key Insights

Men’s Progression: Male runners showed a substantial average improvement of 1 minute and 12 seconds, dropping from an average freshman time of 19:34 to 18:22 as seniors, with 87% running faster in their final year.
Women’s Progression: Female runners showed a more modest average improvement of 9 seconds, moving from 22:36 as freshmen to 22:28 as seniors, with 59% improving their times.
Interactive Exploration: The project features interactive stacked dotplots where readers can hover over individual runners to trace their personal performance progression between freshman and senior year.

title: Cross Country Courses
text:
Featured Ohio Cross Country Courses
Explore 10 distinct cross country courses across Ohio where high school athletes compete, featuring the runner, their recorded race time and year, and an example of the race conditions that day.






1. Cedarville University (Elvin R. King Course)

Runner: Elias Bezy (Lehman Catholic)
Year: 2018
5K Time: 19:40
Course Conditions: Rolling grass terrain with two gradual inclines; firm footing, open and breezy.











2. Lorain County Community College Course

Runner: Ryan Cummings (No. Olmsted)
Year: 2016
5K Time: 18:25
Course Conditions: Wooded trails that turned slick and muddy after morning rain; tight turns through the trees.











3. Battelle Darby Creek Metro Park

Runner: Micaila Mountain (Grove City)
Year: 2012
5K Time: 22:56
Course Conditions: Wide, flat prairie grass trails; dry, firm ground, flat and fast.











4. Voice of America MetroPark

Runner: Casey Murphy (Bellbrook)
Year: 2015
5K Time: 21:45
Course Conditions: Manicured turf and gravel paths around the lake; wide-open, flat, and very fast.











5. Edgewater Park (Cleveland Metroparks)

Runner: Eliza Clark (Seven Hills)
Year: 2013
5K Time: 24:53
Course Conditions: Open grassy hills along the lakefront; brisk headwinds off Lake Erie with firm turf footing.











6. Hedges-Boyer Park (Tiffin)

Runner: Mattie Lunceford (Plymouth)
Year: 2012
5K Time: 22:44
Course Conditions: Historic hilly course featuring the steep “Beast” hill; soft turf with muddy footing near creek crossings.











7. Fortress Obetz

Runner: Ricky Dungan (Wilmington)
Year: 2018
5K Time: 18:23
Course Conditions: Championship stadium course; wide spectator-lined straightaways, gravel mounds, and fast manicured turf.











8. Sharon Woods Metro Park

Runner: Ryan Cooper (Batavia)
Year: 2014
5K Time: 17:50
Course Conditions: Scenic lakeside loop with gentle rolling hills; well-packed dirt and crushed gravel under crisp autumn skies.











9. Scioto Grove Metro Park

Runner: Kristina Nusbaum (Carey)
Year: 2012
5K Time: 22:13
Course Conditions: Open savanna and river bluffs; uneven prairie grass paths with damp, soft turf in low sections.











10. Blendon Woods Metro Park

Runner: Natalie Fleming (Woodridge)
Year: 2016
5K Time: 19:29
Course Conditions: Dense fall forest trails and rolling ravines; leaf-covered dirt paths with slick roots and tight turns.
